Where it began

Ryan Rickelton was born in Perth on 11 July 1996. He came up through Gauteng, making his first-class debut for them against Northerns and his first Twenty20 appearance in the Africa T20 Cup in September 2017.

The 2017–18 season showed what he could do. He was Gauteng's leading run-scorer in the one-day competition, with 351 runs in eight matches, and in the three-day cup as well, with 562 in six. A place in the Cricket South Africa Emerging Squad followed in 2018.

The player

He kept knocking on the door. In 2021 he toured Zimbabwe with South Africa A and topped the run charts in the one-day series with 224, including a hundred. He was named in Test squads against India and for the tour of New Zealand before his debut finally came against Bangladesh on 31 March 2022. His first one-day international followed against the West Indies in March 2023, and he was in South Africa's squad for the 2024 T20 World Cup.

By November 2026 he had played 18 Tests and scored 1,073 runs at 37.00, with three hundreds and one fifty. Behind the stumps he had taken nine catches, with seven more in the field.

What made him special

His best day came at Newlands in January 2025, against Pakistan, when he made 259, his first double hundred in Test cricket. Later that year he was part of the South African team that won the World Test Championship final.

There was a curious shape to his record. By November 2026 he had made more Test hundreds than fifties, which suggests that once he got going he did not much like to stop.

Away from the middle

He showed he could lead, too, captaining the Imperial Lions in the CSA T20 Challenge in 2022. That same year he spent time in England with Northamptonshire in the County Championship. At home he turned out for the Jozi Stars in the Mzansi Super League and for MI Cape Town, so he was well used to new dressing rooms and new team-mates.

And finally

Rickelton was patient about his chance. Twice he was named in a Test squad without getting a game, and his cap came at the third time of asking. After that he made up for lost time, and 259 in a single innings is a fair way of catching up.
